title: とは限らない — “not necessarily ～”
summary: Plain form + とは限らない means “it is not always the case that ～; not necessarily ～.” It denies a general belief, saying there are exceptions. It is often used with 必ずしも or いつも.

patterns.form: 普通形 ＋ とは限らない
patterns.gloss: plain form + とは限らない (いいとは限らない)

patterns.form: 必ずしも ＋ 普通形 ＋ とは限らない
patterns.gloss: 必ずしも…とは限らない: not always (emphasized)

body.p: 限る means “to limit.” とは限らない says that something is not limited to being true. 高いものがいいとは限らない (Expensive things are not necessarily good). With nouns and な-adjectives, だ is dropped: 有名な店が必ずおいしいとは限らない.
It does not deny completely; it means there are cases when it is true and cases when it is not. For a total denial, you would use ～ない or 決して〜ない.
必ずしも is often added to stress the “not always” meaning: 必ずしも正しいとは限らない. It is common in opinions and essays.

examples.ja: 高（たか）いものがいいとは限（かぎ）らない。
examples.romaji: Takai mono ga ii towa kagiranai.

examples.ja: 有名（ゆうめい）な店（みせ）が、必（かなら）ずおいしいとは限（かぎ）らない。
examples.romaji: Yūmei na mise ga, kanarazu oishii towa kagiranai.
examples.tr: A famous restaurant isn't necessarily delicious.

examples.ja: お金（かね）があれば幸（しあわ）せだとは限（かぎ）らない。
examples.romaji: Okane ga areba shiawase da towa kagiranai.
examples.tr: Having money doesn't necessarily mean you are happy.

pitfalls: It only denies “always.” To say something never happens, do not use it.
Do not use it for the speaker's own plan or wish. It is a general statement.
